content.text:
The pattern fits CaLaFeWO6 (mp-1646508) alone; I found no clear sign of a second phase.

I simulated three of the nine candidates, all perovskite-type: mp-1646508, mp-1218565 and mp-1227151. I matched shapes by eye over these regions, without fitting the profiles.

- **19–20°:** The observed pattern has a broad double hump, stronger on the low-angle side. The mp-1646508 simulation shows the same double peak.
- **31–33° (strongest group):** The observed pattern has a cluster of several peaks, with the strongest near 32.5°. The mp-1646508 simulation reproduces this cluster's profile almost peak for peak.
- **Weaker features:** A small peak near 23° and a cluster around 35–36° also have counterparts in mp-1646508.
- **Other simulated candidates:** mp-1218565 gives a single sharp main peak near 32°, and mp-1227151 has a different peak layout, so neither matches as well.

I did not simulate the other six candidates. Two of them, a spinel-type and a rock-salt-type structure, seemed unlikely from their expected peak positions. I also did not check every small feature above about 40°, so a minor second phase can't be fully ruled out.

{"present": ["mp-1646508"], "confidence": 0.85, "note": "The simulated CaLaFeWO6 peaks (19-20 degree double hump, 31-33 degree multiplet, 35-36 degree group) match the observed pattern by eye, and no second phase is clearly needed."}
